timers_disabled.text: A Tokio 1.x context was found, but timers are disabled. Call `enable_time` on the runtime builder to enable timers.

mark_pending.text: mark_pending called when the timer entry is in an invalid state

findings.question: Open edge 2 of research/work-items/RE-005-node115-park-timeout-provenance, restated there as: the writers of the time context fields the forwarder reads -- the wheel state at ctx+0x58, the base pair at ctx+0x88/+0x90, the shutdown byte at ctx+0x80, and the adjusted budget stored to ctx+0x78 -- and the forwarder exit path's call through 0x5ceaa20, which recomputes the remaining period itself, are not traced.  The park-unpark writer packet (PR #2945) left the same fields in the same form.  This packet settles all five.
findings.identity: SETTLED.  The forwarder's ctx is the time half of the combined driver value built by driver_ctor 0x5ce01f0: ctx = value + 0x40.  Under that shift the constructor's stores land exactly on the fields the consumers read -- value+0x90 is the byte lock at ctx+0x50 (stored 0 at pin 0x5ce04eb), the 0x20-byte wheel state copied to value+0x91..0xb1 puts its levels pointer at value+0x98 = ctx+0x58, elapsed at ctx+0x60, pending-list links at ctx+0x68/+0x70, the deadline cache store at value+0xb8 = ctx+0x78, the shutdown byte at value+0xc0 = ctx+0x80 and the base pair at value+0xc8/+0xd0 = ctx+0x88/+0x90.  Every independent route confirms the same shift: registration_a and the signal body reach the state at scheduler-context + 0x1c0 (value at +0x180; add pin 0x5cfb7e1, signal add pin 0x5cfc200), registration_b at [[T]+0x10] + 0x160 (value at +0x120; displacement pin 0x5cec92b), and the timer entry cancel body at owner + 0x160 or owner + 0x240 (value at +0x120/+0x200; pins 0x5ceafdc/0x5ceafe1).  The same object also hosts the io state below +0x50: the io wake body 0x5cef000, tail-called by the shutdown setter, operates [ctx+8], [ctx+0x10] and the [ctx+0x44] token the selectors test.
findings.base_pair: SETTLED, one writer.  driver_ctor's fresh arm tests the config time-flag byte: set (supply pin 0x5ce03fe, clock call pin 0x5ce0403) it calls clock 0x5c842e0 once and stores secs to value+0xc8 (pin 0x5ce0531) and nanos to value+0xd0 (pin 0x5ce0538) -- the pair is the driver's construction instant.  Clear, the value tag is 2 (pin 0x5ce0438) and the nanos word is the sentinel 0x3b9aca00 (pin 0x5ce043d): the "timers disabled" encoding.  Every consumer tests that word before touching any other field -- the forwarder at entry (pin 0x5cfdd0e, panic time/mod.rs:214), the shutdown setter (pin 0x5ce091a, panic time/mod.rs:190), the cancel body (pin 0x5ceafea, panic time/entry.rs:549) -- so in the disabled flavour the secs slot (which then holds the constructor's companion-Arc pointer) is never read.  The constructor's third arm (tag 3, store pin 0x5ce06a4) wraps an already-built context and does not rewrite the pair.
findings.wheel_state: SETTLED.  The 0x20-byte wheel state {levels, elapsed, list head, list tail} is built only by wheel_ctor 0x5cf6480, whose only caller in the artifact is driver_ctor (call pin 0x5ce0412; census).  It stores a fresh levels buffer from levels_alloc 0x5ce1050 (call pin 0x5cf648f; the buffer is 6 level records of 0x410 bytes, the stride wheel_resolve and wheel_process index by), elapsed = 0 (pin 0x5cf649a), the levels pointer (pin 0x5cf64a2) and a zeroed pending list (pin 0x5cf64a8); driver_ctor copies the result into the value (pins 0x5ce0502/0x5ce0518).  After construction the levels pointer is never rewritten.  The elapsed field is advanced only by wheel_process 0x5cf6510 (monotonic stores at pins 0x5cf6607/0x5cf677d), which is called only by the unlock body (call pin 0x5ceaa76; census); the pending-list links are mutated by wheel_process and the entry cancel/insert paths under the ctx lock.
findings.shutdown_byte: SETTLED, one runtime writer.  The byte starts 0 (driver_ctor store pin 0x5ce052a).  shutdown_setter 0x5ce08e0 xchg's 1 into [ctx+0x80] (pin 0x5ce093d) after reading the byte and returning early when it is already set (pin 0x5ce0926), after the timers-enabled check on [ctx+0x90] (pin 0x5ce091a; Location time/mod.rs line 190 col 32, static 0x64c6fa8).  It then calls the unlock body with an elapsed of -1 (pin 0x5ce0950) and tail-calls the io wake body 0x5cef000.  The setter has exactly two callers in the artifact (census): the drop body 0x5ceb330 (call pin 0x5ceb47e, ctx passed as its second argument + 0x150) and the current_thread signal body 0x5cfbfd0 (call pin 0x5cfc20d, ctx = its object + 0x1c0).  No other body in the closed method set stores to the byte.
findings.budget_cache: SETTLED, three writers, no reader.  driver_ctor initialises value+0xb8 = 0 (pin 0x5ce051f).  The forwarder stores the wheel_resolve budget it computed to [ctx+0x78] while holding the lock (pin 0x5cfdd7a; the value's provenance is #2938's settled cap).  The unlock body stores its own re-resolved deadline to [state+0x28] = ctx+0x78 (pin 0x5ceabc4) on every exit.  Both runtime stores write the resolver's result word (+carry) for the same wheel state.  No body in the method set -- forwarder, unlock, wheel process/resolver, setter, cancel, insert -- ever loads the slot: the next deadline is always recomputed from the wheel, so in this artifact ctx+0x78 is a write-only cache.
findings.exit_recompute: SETTLED.  The body on the forwarder's exit path, 0x5ceaa20, is the state's unlock/process body: its self pointer is &ctx+0x50 (the lock byte is its +0, the wheel its +8), it has exactly two references (census) -- the shutdown setter's call with elapsed = -1 and the forwarder's tail jump at 0x5cfe088 with elapsed = milliseconds since the base instant.  It takes the lock (pin 0x5ceaa47), caps the elapsed argument at the wheel's current elapsed field, advances the wheel through wheel_process (pin 0x5ceaa76), drains expired entries into a WakeList (overflow panics at util/wake_list.rs lines 35/36), re-resolves the wheel (pin 0x5ceaba7) and stores the next deadline to ctx+0x78 (pin 0x5ceabc4), then releases the lock and fires the collected wakers.  This closes the second half of the #2938 open edge: the exit recompute is the same remaining-period computation, run under the lock on the way out.
findings.forwarder_use: Connection to the settled cap (#2938): the base pair is the construction instant in the clock body's (secs, nanos) domain, and the wheel's millisecond values (elapsed, budgets, deadlines) live in the same domain starting from 0 at construction.  The forwarder's elapsed = instant_sub(clock now, base pair) is therefore the time since the driver was built, and remaining = budget - elapsed is the time left in the current wheel period measured from construction -- the writers above are what make the two sides of that subtraction commensurable.

open_edges: The tag-3 arm of driver_ctor wraps an already-built context (its fields were written by an earlier fresh construction); which runtime build paths supply it, and whether a wrapped context's fields can ever be re-initialised afterwards, is not traced here.

The drop body passes ctx as (its second argument) + 0x150.  The object that argument points into is not identified in this packet; the value passed satisfies the same field contract, but the +0x150 base relation to the +0x160/+0x1c0 forms is stated as observed, not derived.

The insert path (insert_body 0x5cea7c0 via wheel_insert 0x5cf6880) writes wheel level slots and entry fields, and the pending-list links at ctx+0x68/+0x70 are mutated by the entry paths under the lock; a full field census of the insert path is not part of this packet.  Its stores do not land on any of the five fields settled here.

Whether the disabled flavour's base secs slot can be observed by any path that skips the sentinel check is a whole-artifact negative this packet does not claim: every traced consumer checks the nanos word first, and the claim is limited to them.
The io half of the same object (fields below ctx+0x50, including the [ctx+0x44] token) belongs to the io driver graph of the TLS value-object and timeout-pair packets and is not re-traced here.
